issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 9-12), but the solution defines a different initializer init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 14-16) while the solution's Client calls Bookstore(books: books) (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift lines 31-58). This constructor parameter mismatch creates a structural conflict: students following the problem spec will implement the single-parameter initializer, yet the solution contains a different signature, and the solution's own usage assumes the single-parameter form. This inconsistency can confuse students about the required initializer and will prevent code from compiling if the wrong signature is used.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's initializer to init(books: [Book]) so it matches the problem statement and the Client usage, or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) and ensure Client and tests are updated accordingly. The simplest fix is to remove the extra 'valid: Bool' parameter from the solution initializer (or provide an overload/init with defaulted parameter) so all references use init(books: [Book]).

issues.description: The problem statement requires an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) for the Bookstore class, but the solution implementation declares an initializer with an additional parameter init(books: [Book], valid: Bool). This introduces an unexpected parameter name ('valid') and changes the expected API surface. Students mapping the requirement to the implementation will be confused about which initializer to implement and which parameters are required. The solution's Client also calls Bookstore(books: books) while the Bookstore initializer in the solution requires the extra 'valid' parameter, creating a contradiction between the usage and the declared initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Bookstore initializer across artifacts. Either remove the extra 'valid: Bool' parameter from the solution initializer so it matches init(books: [Book]), or update the problem statement (and any template comments) to require init(books: [Book], valid: Bool). Ensure the Client usage and any tests also match the chosen initializer signature.
